title: A codon is three nucleotides; there are 64 triplets and 20 standard amino acids
summary: OpenStax states the triplet arithmetic. The National Human Genome Research Institute describes codons as specifying amino acids.
body: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 15.1, says each amino acid is specified by a three-nucleotide codon, that there are 16 possible pairs and 64 possible triplets, and it displays the 20 amino acids found in proteins. The National Human Genome Research Institute's glossary says the bases spell three-letter codons that specify which amino acid is needed at each position in a protein. The v1 claim that the code is "nearly universal" with known exceptions was not on the glossary text we fetched, so exceptions are not asserted here.
said_by: OpenStax Biology 2e and the National Human Genome Research Institute
